question.text: A PM's portfolio has a max drawdown of 22% over the last 5 years. This means:

answer.text: The portfolio lost exactly 22% on one day
The largest peak-to-trough decline in portfolio NAV was 22%

explanation.text: The Logic: Max drawdown = largest peak-to-trough decline over the measurement period. Shows the worst historical pain experienced. The Trap: Not a daily loss; not volatility (which is σ of returns, not peak-to-trough). Cross-Exam Context: XV, X-A all mention drawdown; XXI-B tests as risk measure. Manager's Pro-Tip: Drawdown recovery time (how long to reach prior peak) is often more painful for clients than the size itself — report both.
